prompt:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac1x$, $x\neq0$.

**(a)** Show that $f$ is its own inverse. **[1]**

**(b)** Explain how this is shown by the graph of $y=f(x)$. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $f(f(x))=\dfrac{1}{1/x}=x$, so $f^{-1}=f$ **(A1)**

**(b)** The hyperbola $y=\frac1x$ is symmetric in the line $y=x$, so reflecting it in $y=x$ leaves it unchanged **(R1)**

The graph of $y=\dfrac{ax+3}{x+b}$ has asymptotes $x=2$ and $y=-4$. Find $a$ and $b$.
markscheme: Vertical asymptote where $x+b=0$: $b=-2$ **(A1)**; horizontal asymptote $y=\dfrac a1$: $a=-4$ **(A1)**
